"Do braces or aligners cause TMJ problems? The answer is: No." Braces and clear aligners do not cause TMJ/TMD. Research has consistently shown that orthodontic treatment is not a cause of temporomandibular disorders (TMD). If someone develops jaw pain during treatment, it's usually because TMD is a common condition that can appear with or without braces. Factors like stress, teeth grinding (bruxism), muscle overuse, previous jaw injuries, and existing joint issues are much more likely contributors. Orthodontic treatment is designed to improve your bite and smile—not to cause TMJ disorders. If you have jaw pain, clicking, or difficulty opening your mouth, don't panic. A proper evaluation can identify the real cause and guide the right treatment. Don't let myths stop you from getting the smile you deserve.

That’s not the real question. 👀 The real question is — who is planning and monitoring your treatment? Every person’s bone density, gum health, bite force, and tooth movement speed are different. That’s why the same aligner plan can give completely different results for two people. Scientifically, aligners work through controlled force systems. But if that force is not monitored properly, teeth may stop tracking, move unpredictably, or create bite issues over time. Premium systems usually invest more in: • Better material elasticity • More accurate digital simulations • Predictable force delivery • Advanced treatment planning software But even the best aligner system can fail without proper orthodontic supervision. A successful smile transformation is a mix of: ✔️ Correct diagnosis ✔️ Smart biomechanics ✔️ Regular monitoring ✔️ Timely refinements So don’t choose aligners based only on marketing or price. Choose the system — and the doctor — that understands your biology, not just your smile. ✨ #smilesbydrravneet #clearaligners #orthodontics #smilescience #dentalawareness aligner treatment science, how clear aligners work, orthodontic treatment planning

When Should Your Child See an Orthodontist? You don't always have to wait until all of your child's permanent teeth have erupted before seeing an orthodontist. For some children, an orthodontic evaluation between 6 and 10 years of age can help identify growth and bite concerns at an important stage of development. Look out for signs such as: Mouth breathing or frequent snoring Crowded or misplaced teeth Crossbite A narrow upper jaw Concerns with the bite or jaw growth Early evaluation doesn't necessarily mean your child needs braces. It allows an orthodontist to monitor development and, when appropriate, guide jaw growth or use expansion while your child is still growing. If something doesn't look right with your child's bite, jaw, teeth, or breathing, don't wait for all the permanent teeth to come in. An early checkup can help identify problems while there is still an opportunity to guide growth. Want to know the 5 signs your child may need an orthodontic checkup? Here's what can happen if you keep using an old toothbrush: 🦷 Your teeth don't get cleaned as effectively. 🦷 Plaque can build up more easily. 🦷 Your risk of cavities and gum problems may increase. 🦷 Stains and bad breath can become more noticeable. A simple rule to remember: ✅ Replace your toothbrush (or electric toothbrush head) every 3 months. ✅ Change it sooner if the bristles are frayed. ✅ Replace it after recovering from a cold, flu, or other illness. A new toothbrush takes just a minute to replace, but it can make a big difference to your daily oral hygiene and long-term dental health.
